title: Structured outputs and bad inputs: errors as data

concept.heading: A tool never raises; it returns an error the model can act on
paragraphs: The model will ask for a donor that does not exist, pass a date in the wrong format, call the same tool twice, and invent a tool name. Each of those is a normal Tuesday, not a bug. If the handler raises, the loop dies and the staff member sees nothing. If the handler returns {"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": ..., "suggestion": ...}}, the model reads it like any other result and recovers: tells the user, tries the last name, stops.

The registry is where this happens. ToolRegistry.call validates arguments against the pydantic model (invalid_arguments, naming the fields), maps a DonorNotFound to not_found, a CrmError to upstream_error, and an unknown name to unknown_tool with the list of real names. The handlers stay simple; the registry is the one place that promises never to raise.

One case belongs to the loop: the model repeating an identical call in the same run. Executing it again would double a write. The loop returns a duplicate_call error instead, which is the first idempotency rule in this track; Module 4 makes it durable.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Configure run after: has failed, the scope with a catch branch, and the Terminate action with a custom message. The difference: here the error goes back to the model as data, so the assistant can keep working instead of the flow ending.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: try/except with specific exceptions, pydantic ValidationError, dict equality
pythonBlock.intro: Catch the narrowest exception you can name, and turn it into data at the boundary.

spec: Implement error_result and is_error in tools/errors.py exactly to the documented shape.

Implement ToolRegistry.call: unknown_tool (details.available), invalid_arguments (details.fields), not_found for DonorNotFound (details.donor_id), upstream_error for CrmError and for any httpx connection failure. It never raises.
In run_loop, when a tool call repeats the name and arguments of one already executed in this run, do not execute it; append a duplicate_call error result instead.
An empty find_donor match is a normal result with matches 0, not an error. Decide why, and write that reasoning into the description if it is not there.
askClaudeFor: The list of exceptions httpx can raise on a dead host and which of them your upstream_error branch must catch.
A review of your error messages: would a model (or a staff member reading the transcript) know what to do next?
writeYourself: The duplicate-call guard in the loop.
